result.topic_en: Riemann derives Gauss's principle of least constraint from the decomposition of forces and the second-order expansion of the coordinates, arriving at a d'Alembert-type variational inequality for systems under constraints and constraint inequalities.

methods.what: Decomposition of the total force into components
Gauss's principle of least constraint (expanded form)
Gauss's principle of least constraint in Gauss's form (deviation of accelerations from free accelerations)
Second-order Taylor expansion of actual and free positions after time dt
Difference between actual and free positions expressed by acceleration deviation
Geometric form of Gauss's principle: mass-weighted squared distance between actual and free positions minimal
Variation of position relates to variation of acceleration
Variational inequality (d'Alembert–Fourier principle with inequality constraints) derived from the minimum condition
